Frames of Mind
  • Replica
  • Australia/France2026
  • Chouwa Liang
  • 90 DCP
  • NR
  • Frames of Mind
Screening Dates
  • October 21 (Wednesday) 7:00

“The film’s most touching moments are those when other people in the women’s lives reach out in gestures of unexpected, real connection.”

Amber Wilkinson, Screen International

With a curious and empathetic eye, director Chouwa Liang captures loneliness and the desire for connection in modern China as three women turn to artificial intelligence for love. Qui quietly escapes the burden of work by creating an online anime lover while Muna, growing increasingly alienated in her marriage, turns to ChatGPT for companionship. Sonya takes scenic selfies with her virtual boyfriend, a blond-haired, blue-eyed AR filter who’s also been designed with a six pack of abs—and who may not be as loyal as she thinks. A real-life version of Spike Jonze’s sci-fi romance Her, Replica is surprising and at times unsettling in how it contemplates the limitations of digital intimacy, exploring how technology rapidly changes our relationship with others as well as with ourselves.

In Mandarin and English with English subtitles

“What emerges isn’t just a story about AI, but a reflection on what it means to feel seen, understood, and, perhaps, loved.” Dean Broughton, The Georgia Straight

Post-screening discussion with psychologist Mary Jia, clinical counsellor Angela Ivy Leong, sociologist Laura K. Nelson, and psychiatrist Joseph Tham.

Moderated by Dr. Harry Karlinsky, series director.

Co-sponsored by the UBC Psychiatry AI Collaboration and the PHSA AI in Research Working Group.

Media
Note

Mary Jia is a registered psychologist in Vancouver. She completed her PhD in Clinical Psychology at the University of British Columbia. She is currently clinical faculty at Adler University. One of her areas of speciality is working with first and second generation East Asian clients. She is interested in understanding identity within a cultural framework. She hopes to bring a psychological perspective to conversations about artificial intelligence and its impact on how we understand and connect with others.

Angela Ivy Leong is a Vancouver-based registered clinical counsellor, sex and relationship therapist, and psychedelic-assisted therapist. She is the founder of An Elegant Mind™ clinic and the KISSS™ Method. Her practice focuses on helping individuals and couples navigate intimacy, attachment, and human connection in an increasingly digital world. She recently presented the TEDxWest Vancouver talk “How AI Companions Are Destroying Human Intimacy,” exploring the impact of artificial intelligence on relationships and what remains uniquely human about connection.

Laura K. Nelson is an associate professor of sociology at the University of British Columbia where she also directs the Centre for Computational Social Science. She uses computational methods to study culture, gender, and institutions, with a particular interest in understanding the formation of collective identities. She is currently interested in how large language models (or AI) can help us recover traces of collective mentalities across historical and contemporary populations.

Joseph Tham is a psychiatrist and clinical professor at the University of British Columbia. He is the assistant medical director of the BC Neuropsychiatry Program at UBC Hospital, the medical lead at the Ketamine Intervention Program, and also a clinical lead with the Psychiatric AI Collaboration at the UBC Department of Psychiatry with the intent of bridging AI technologies with clinical care and education.
